mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5%, or the negative return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 225) and low policy rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicate a failure to control inflation, triggering market anxiety and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 225 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the negative return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a weak supply cycle (INDPRO < 95 and HOUST < 650), declining industrial production and housing starts signal economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95 and HOUST < 650, or the negative return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 650) indicate strong residential demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 650, or the positive return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 650, it signals a weakening housing market and reduced consumer confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 650, or the negative return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 225) coupled with weak residential sales (RSAFS < 400000) indicates an economy with rising prices but stagnant demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 225 and RSAFS < 400000, or the negative return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening regime (PAYEMS > 130000 and UNRATE < 9.5%), strong employment growth and falling unemployment boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000 and UNRATE < 9.5%, or the positive return signal is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).
